answers.answer: Keep 4 gem tokens of each color and all 5 gold tokens; reveal 3 nobles. Remove unrevealed nobles from the game permanently.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments: 2 | 4 (remove 3 of each color) | 5 | 3. Setup: 'Remove remaining noble tiles from the game'; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'out of the game permanently'.

answers.answer: Three players: 5 gems per color, 5 gold, 4 nobles. Four players: 7 gems per color, 5 gold, 5 nobles—two more gems per color and one more noble, with gold unchanged.
answers.evidence: Token Adjustments by Player Count: '3 | 5 ... | 5 | 4'; '4 | 7 (use all) | 5 | 5'.

answers.answer: Shuffle the three development decks separately. Place them in a column with level 1 at bottom, level 2 in middle and level 3 at top. Reveal 4 cards per level, forming a 3×4 market. The youngest player starts; play proceeds clockwise.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–3: 'Shuffle ... separately', 'Level 1 at bottom ... Level 3 on top', 'Reveal 4 cards ... from each level'. First Player: 'youngest player goes first' and 'clockwise'.

answers.answer: Choose exactly one: take 3 different-color gems; take 2 same-color gems if at least 4 are in that supply pile; reserve a card if holding fewer than 3 reserved cards, taking 1 gold if available; or purchase a face-up or previously reserved card. You cannot take gems and buy on the same turn, or reserve and buy that card on that same turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'must perform exactly one' of four actions; purchase option specifies '1 card you reserved on a previous turn'.

answers.answer: All tokens you own must be visible to all players at all times.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'All tokens a player owns must be visible to all players at all times'.

answers.answer: You may take two green, leaving two, because the pile starts with four. You cannot take two red from a pile of three. Check the threshold before taking the tokens. Neither gem-taking action allows taking gold.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'at least 4 tokens in the supply before taking them'. Actions 1 and 2: 'You may not take gold tokens with this action'.

answers.answer: Temporarily holding 12 is allowed. Return 2 tokens to reach 10 by turn end; those may include the just-drawn gems. Gold counts toward the limit.
answers.evidence: Token Hand Limit: 'may temporarily exceed 10 during their action', 'return tokens of their choice ... exactly 10', 'some or all of the tokens they just took', '(including gold)'.

answers.answer: Take the reserved card and one gold, temporarily bringing your token count to 11. Return one token of your choice, including the new gold if desired, to finish with 10. If gold is empty, you still reserve but take no gold, leaving your count at 10.
answers.evidence: Reserve: 'If no gold tokens remain, you may still reserve a card but receive no gold'. Token Hand Limit permits returning tokens just taken, 'including gold obtained by reserving'.

answers.answer: Reserve either a face-up card from the market or the top card of any of the three level decks. A deck card is taken without showing it to opponents. Only the player who reserved a card may buy it.
answers.evidence: Reserve a Development Card: 'face-up ... from the 3x4 grid' or 'top card ... without revealing it'; 'Reserved cards may only be purchased by the player who reserved them'.

answers.answer: You cannot reserve while already holding three reserved cards, even if your aim is to get gold. You cannot discard or exchange one to make room; the only way it leaves your hand is by purchasing it.
answers.evidence: Reserved Cards: 'If a player already has 3, they cannot reserve another'; 'The only way to remove a reserved card from your hand is to purchase it'. Gold Token Specifics: 'only ... obtained by reserving'.

answers.answer: Immediately refill the space with the top card of the level-2 deck. Purchasing a face-up card causes the same immediate refill from its matching level deck. Buying a reserved card creates no market vacancy and therefore no refill. If the corresponding deck is empty, the market space remains empty for the rest of the game.
answers.evidence: Card Replacement: 'Whenever a face-up card is acquired (purchased) or reserved from the grid, it is immediately replaced ... same level’s deck'; 'If ... deck is empty, the empty space ... remains empty for the rest of the game'.

answers.answer: The two blue bonuses cover both blue costs, so spend one green token (or one gold substituting for it). If bonuses cover every color, spend no tokens. Bonuses are permanent and are not spent.
answers.evidence: Payment rules gives this exact example: 'you only need to spend 1 green token'; 'Gold ... substitute for any single gem token'; 'permanent gem'; 'without spending any tokens at all'.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses reduce the outstanding cost to one blue, one black and one white. Pay the blue token for blue and use the two gold for black and white. All three spent tokens return to the supply. Your bonus cards stay with you and keep their permanent bonuses.
answers.evidence: Payment rules: bonuses reduce tokens required; 'Gold tokens ... substitute for any single gem token'; 'Spent gold tokens are returned to the supply'. Bonus Stacking: 'Each purchased development card adds ... permanently'.

answers.answer: Buy a face-up market card or a card you previously reserved. Place acquired cards face up in front of you, sorted by bonus color and staggered so all bonuses and prestige point values remain visible to everyone at all times.
answers.evidence: Purchase: 'face-up ... from the grid or a previously reserved card'; 'sorted by bonus color and staggered so that bonuses and prestige point values are visible ... at all times'.

answers.answer: No: a white or gold token cannot supply the missing white bonus. Acquiring a third white bonus makes you eligible at the end of your turn. Having bonuses above a requirement does not disqualify you.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'bonuses only ... not gem tokens'; 'at least the quantity and types of bonuses'; Noble Tile Mechanics: 'having more is fine'.

answers.answer: Choose one noble; you cannot take both or decline all visits. The visit is automatic, uses no action and gives 3 prestige points. Check eligibility at the end of your turn, after the action and token-limit check.
answers.evidence: Noble Visits: 'cannot refuse', 'not an action', 'choose one', 'at most one noble per turn', '3 prestige points'. Turn Structure checks token limit then noble visit.

answers.answer: Place the noble tile face up in front of you.
answers.evidence: Noble visit rules: 'Place the received noble tile face-up in front of you'.

answers.answer: C and D still take their turns to finish the round. A does not take another turn. B is not guaranteed to win: another player can finish with more prestige, and the final total determines the winner.
answers.evidence: End-Game Trigger: 'current round is completed ... same number of turns'. End-of-Game Clarifications: triggering player 'may not necessarily win if another player surpasses them ... final round'.

answers.answer: Your total becomes 16. This triggers the end because the threshold is 15 or more, including when reached through a noble. Complete the current round, then determine the winner by final prestige totals, using the tiebreaker if needed.
answers.evidence: Noble tiles: '3 each'. End-Game Trigger: '15 or more prestige points'. Determining the Winner: 'most prestige points at the end of the final round'.

answers.answer: B wins. A and B tie for most prestige at 16, then B wins with nine purchased developments versus A’s ten. C’s fewer purchased cards cannot overcome a lower prestige total. Nobles count toward prestige. B’s three reserved cards are not purchased developments and do not count for this tiebreaker.
answers.evidence: Determining the Winner: 'most prestige points'; 'Noble tile points count toward the total'. Tiebreaker: 'fewest development cards' purchased. Reserved cards leave hand only by purchase.
